headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 13 of the 19 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Quiet and dry weather is expected through the late week.
Dry and seasonable conditions continue through next weekend.

ALY.excerpt: ) Dry weather will persist across eastern New York and western New England with high pressure in control through the week, while a Nor'easter meanders well offshore.

GYX.excerpt: High pressure remains in control for the rest of the week into the weekend with little to no precipitation on the horizon.

PHI.excerpt:
A nor'easter well off the Mid-Atlantic coast will bring coastal impacts and hazardous marine conditions through about Thursday.
A prolonged period of onshore flow will lead to multiple elevated high tide cycles this week resulting in rounds of coastal flooding.

CTP.excerpt: ) Extended stretch of dry and seasonable weather this week

RLX.excerpt: ) High pressure ruling the roost through the weekend will continue to advertise dry weather and cool overnight temperatures.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:24}} to {{t:51}}, mostly dry.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 29).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Monday 7:47 PM: "Quiet and dry weather is expected through the late week."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.
